nav.heartClock: Heart clock: ECG and the cardiac cycle
heartClock.title: Heart clock
heartClock.intro: One timer drives the whole cardiac cycle. The ECG below is generated from it: change the heart rate and watch the waves and the phases of the cycle follow.
heartClock.ecgLabel: Synthetic ECG, one lead. Grid: 25 mm per second, 10 mm per millivolt.
heartClock.ecgDescription: Sinus rhythm at {rate} beats per minute. Each beat has a P wave, then a narrow QRS complex, then a T wave, and the intervals between beats are equal.
heartClock.schematic: A schematic teaching model, not a recording and not for diagnosis. Not reviewed by a physician. Durations follow published averages and are simplified; some values are model assumptions.
heartClock.wiggers.title: Wiggers diagram
heartClock.wiggers.label: Wiggers diagram: pressure in the left ventricle, aorta and left atrium, left ventricular volume and the ECG over one cardiac cycle, with a cursor at the current moment.
heartClock.wiggers.description: During ventricular systole the pressure in the left ventricle rises above the aortic pressure and blood is ejected, so the ventricular volume falls. After the aortic valve closes the pressure in the ventricle drops below the atrial pressure, the mitral valve opens and the ventricle fills again; atrial contraction adds the last part of the filling.
